To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
peptide dendrimers can be synthesized by combinatorial synthesis and selected for catalytic activity.
a 65,536 member combinatorial library was prepared by split and mix synthesis and screened on a solid support for esterase activity.
peptide dendrimers can be prepared as a 65,536 member library by split-and-mine synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a combinatorial approach to the identification of active sequences from large peptide libraries.
the development of a new class of artificial esterase enzymes based on peptide dendrimers and their application to the synthesis of peptide dendrimer catalysts.
the design, synthesis, and evaluation of enzyme-mimicking peptide dendrimers as catalytic materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the catalytic peptide dendrimer library has provided us with a new class of artificial catalysts with properties similar to those of natural enzymes.
the catalytic properties of the dendrimer are determined by the sequence of the peptide, and that catalysis can be tuned by changing the sequence.
the catalytic peptide dendrimer library is an example of a combinatorial approach to enzyme design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method for the combinatorial synthesis of peptide dendrimiers, and have shown that the resulting dendrimers are capable of catalyzing ester hydrolysis in aqueous buffer.

the combinatorial approach has been successful in identifying catalytically active peptide dendrimers from a 65,536 member library, that these peptide dendrimers have been characterized as esterases, and that they display enzyme-like kinetics and specific rate acceleratiosn.

we have prepared and studied the properties of a 65,536- member combinatorial library for peptide dendrimers, identified active members, synthesized them in solution and purified them by reverse-phase HPL C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalytic peptide dendrimer approach is a viable strategy for the development of enzyme mimics.

the catalytic properties of peptide dendrimes are not significantly different from those of the smaller peptides from which they are derived, despite the large number of residues in the active site of the peptide dendrimer.
combinatorial synthesis, selection, purification, and characterization are possible for catalytically active peptide dendrimers, even in the absence of a template.
